correctness.rationale: Theorem 5.9 of arXiv:2605.00041 describes exactly which compatible pairs occur and which low-rank pairs coincide. Fixing the k-marked partial bijection gives C(n,k)^2 k! choices. The source and target partitions restrict to corresponding marked partitions with q blocks. Their extensions with t unmarked blocks each have U_m(q,t) possibilities, and these blocks admit t! matchings. The subtraction of B_k m! exactly counts those pairs for which every unmarked source point is a singleton. The remaining full-domain exception contributes n! units. Direct enumeration of generator partial maps on T_2 and T_3 gives orders 7 and 106; an unrelated paired-partition enumeration matches ranks through n=5. Proof carefully handles n=1 separately.

value.rationale: The numerical order and distribution by canonical base rank are intrinsic complexity measurements of a finite inverse monoid newly studied in the literature. The explicit count for all degrees n is nontrivial because compatible partial bijections require simultaneous set-partition extension and quotient corrections. The exact next-to-full rank Bell difference provides a compact structural statistic; first orders exhibit growth from 7 to over twenty-six million by degree six. Results are not ad hoc finite computations and naturally support enumeration and algorithmic exploration.
